question: Consider a point source of light emitting spherical wavefronts. Why does the amplitude of the light wave decrease as the distance $r$ from the source increases, unlike a plane wave?

options.A: Because the frequency of the wave decreases with distance
options.B: Because the energy is distributed over an area that increases as $r^2$, so amplitude drops as $1/r$
options.C: Because the speed of light decreases as the wavefront expands
options.D: Because the atmosphere absorbs spherical waves more than plane waves
